publishing_metadata.description:
When they text you back, your phone lights up and your heart skips a beat. Not because their text was poetic—but because you genuinely didn't know if they would reply at all.

You're not falling in love with the person. You're falling in love with the chemical cocktail created by their unpredictability.

In this animated short film, we break down B.F. Skinner's legendary 1950s behavioral experiments, why the human brain releases its biggest spike of dopamine when an outcome is completely uncertain, and why someone who is slightly aloof creates an inescapable psychological gravitational pull.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

01:06 - Dopamine Is Anticipation, Not Pleasure
01:25 - Slot Machines, Lottery Tickets & Notification Badges
01:44 - The Always Available Person (Zero Pull)
02:09 - The Aloof Person in the Dark Hoodie
02:23 - The Compliment That Sticks for Three Weeks
